LESSON: PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 5.1.1: Pronunciation and Vocabulary

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Pronunciation and Vocabulary. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What are some of the new words that you know?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use polite words and phrases in a variety of contexts

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Word reading means looking carefully at a word and saying it correctly.

• Some longer words do not follow simple letter–sound rules. Your teacher models them. You look, listen, then say the word.

• Learn about 8 to 10 new longer words each week. Start with words your teacher shows the class.

• Use word-attack skills when a word is new: look-and-say, find a smaller chunk, find a root word, or cover part of the word and reveal it bit by bit.

• Practise in a group, with a partner, and alone so you become confident.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1 — Look and say: Teacher shows the word “elephant”. Class reads “elephant” together, then in pairs, then one by one.

Example 2 — Word ladder: Write “sun”. Change one letter to make “run”, then “ran”. Say each word as you build the ladder.

Example 3 — Chunking: In “football”, see “foot” + “ball”. In “classroom”, see “class” + “room”.

Example 4 — At home: Open a newspaper or storybook. Pick two long words. Ask a parent to say them, then you repeat and write them.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read five new long words from the board or a chart. Point under each word as you say it.
2. Play a word ladder with a friend: change one letter at a time and read every new word aloud.
3. Find the root or chunks in these words: football, classroom, sunshine, handmade.
4. Choose three new words. Write each word, draw a small picture, and use it in a sentence about school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Copy eight new longer words into your exercise book. Read them to a parent tonight.
2. Make a word ladder of at least four steps. Read it aloud.
3. Answer: How do you read a word you have never seen before?
4. From a newspaper, circle five words you can already read and two that are new. Practise the new ones.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Role-play a telephone conversation, with peers,

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are some of the new words that you know?
2. Why do you enjoy reading some words?
3. How do you read words you have not seen before?
4. How many words can you make from a longer word?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Look at the whole word, then say it clearly.
2. Use chunks, roots, and look-and-say when letter sounds are not enough.
3. Practise new words every week — about eight to ten longer words.
4. Enjoy reading: the more you practise, the easier long words become.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
